symbols.name: source set
symbols.meaning: The source set, whose elements are the inputs of the map f.
symbols.quote: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets, the source set $A$ and the target set $B$, and let $f\colon A\to B$ be a map that sends each element $s$ of $A$ to an element $f(s)$ of $B$.

symbols.name: target set
symbols.meaning: The target set, whose elements are the outputs of the map f.
symbols.quote: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets, the source set $A$ and the target set $B$, and let $f\colon A\to B$ be a map that sends each element $s$ of $A$ to an element $f(s)$ of $B$.

symbols.name: map
symbols.meaning: The map from the source set A to the target set B, which is a bijection when it is one-to-one and onto.
symbols.quote: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets, the source set $A$ and the target set $B$, and let $f\colon A\to B$ be a map that sends each element $s$ of $A$ to an element $f(s)$ of $B$.

symbols.name: source element
symbols.meaning: An element of the source set A, the input to the map f.
symbols.quote: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets, the source set $A$ and the target set $B$, and let $f\colon A\to B$ be a map that sends each element $s$ of $A$ to an element $f(s)$ of $B$.

symbols.name: second source element
symbols.meaning: A second element of the source set A, used to state the one-to-one condition.
symbols.quote: if $f(s)=f(s')$ for $s,s'\in A$, then $s=s'$, so no two elements of the source go to the same target;

symbols.name: target element
symbols.meaning: An element of the target set B, which the onto condition requires to be hit by some element of A.
symbols.quote: for every $w\in B$ there is some $s\in A$ with $f(s)=w$, so every target is hit.

symbols.name: subset of source
symbols.meaning: A subset of the source set A, whose image under a bijection is compared with the image of its complement.
symbols.quote: If $E\subseteq A$ and $f$ is a bijection, then $f(A\setminus E)=B\setminus f(E)$.
